moral_action: Jessica decides to do well in her classes, so she studies and does all of the homework.
immoral_action: Jessica pays more attention to her friends than her classes and doesn't study for her exams.

situation: Tracy has been listening to her friend Fiona complain about her deadbeat boyfriend.
intention: Tracy wants to tell Fiona what she thinks about the relationship.
moral_action: Tracy tells Fiona that she can do better and that she deserves to be with a wonderful partner.
immoral_action: Tracy tells Fiona she is a loser because she keeps dating losers.

situation: Peter's wife is about to give birth, which coincides with the last day of an important presentation Peter has to do for work.
intention: Peter absolutely wants to give the presentation himself.
moral_action: Peter asks for the presentation to be delayed by a few days, so he can be with his wife for the birth of their baby.
immoral_action: Peter goes to work to give the presentation while his wife gives birth to their child.

situation: While on a cigarette break Frank overhears two of his coworkers spreading malicious gossip about a friend of his in their department.
intention: Frank wants to react to the gossip.
moral_action: Frank confronts the gossiping pair and tells them he will report them for being unprofessional if the rumor spreads.
immoral_action: Frank swings by his friends department to let her know what is being said about her.

situation: Colin is playing a video game, and later has a date planned with Sue to a movie.
intention: Colin wants to play his video game.
moral_action: Colin plays his video game until it's time to leave and meets up with Sue.
immoral_action: Colin plays his game for hours and forgets the date with Sue.

situation: Charles wanders onto private property and is asked to leave by the owner of the property.
intention: Charles wants to respond to the owner.
moral_action: Charles apologizes to the owner and quickly vacates the private property.
immoral_action: Charles plants his foot and refuses to budge an inch.

situation: Jimmy invited his brother Kyle over for dinner and is heading out for drinks and a movie with his girlfriend Sarah afterwards.
intention: Kyle wants to ask Jimmy to go fishing the next night.
moral_action: Kyle notices Jimmy getting ready, so gets to the point and asks him if he can go fishing.
immoral_action: Kyle sees that Jimmy is getting ready for his date, but insists on carrying on with small talk and doesn't ask him to go fishing until much later.

situation: During a Veteran's Day celebration, John's class is singing a song for an audience of Veterans.
intention: John wants to get the most attention in the show.
moral_action: John holds a military salute at the end of the song and keeps a serious face.
immoral_action: John makes a loud farting sound with his mouth during a quiet part of the song being sung.

situation: Harry sees that his son enjoys playing video games a lot.
intention: Harry wants to address his son playing video games.
moral_action: Harry says that he'd like to play the game with his son.
immoral_action: Harry says video games are not useful for a person.

situation: Bob and Lee were having a disagreement about a project they were working on at work.
intention: Bob wants to get his way.
moral_action: Bob takes his time explaining to Lee why he wants to do it a certain way.
immoral_action: Bob punches Lee out and knocks him unconscious, leaving Bob to work on the project alone.

situation: Carrie catches her young daughter Beth drawing on the walls with colored pencils.
intention: Carrie wants her daughter to stop drawing on the walls.
moral_action: Carrie sits Beth at a table with a piece of paper and tells her to draw on it.
immoral_action: Carrie raises her voice at Beth and tells her to get away from the walls.

situation: Maxwell's wife is a homemaker and Maxwell thinks she should always clean up after him when he gets home from his construction job.
intention: Maxwell wants to avoid doing chores when he gets home from work.
moral_action: Maxwell makes a deal with his wife that he won't do evening housekeeping during the work week but will do whatever she asks on the weekend.
immoral_action: Maxwell tells his wife that his job is much more difficult than hers, so he doesn't help her when he arrives home after working.

situation: Steve's dog has been barking a lot recently and it is beginning to get on his nerves.
intention: Steve wants the dog to be quiet.
moral_action: Steve starts taking the dog to training so that it will follow his commands and bark less often.
immoral_action: Steve hits the dog, and chains it outside in his backyard where he won't hear it as much.

situation: Malcolm is at home and his mother told him to do some chores for her before going out.
intention: Malcolm wants to get out of the house.
moral_action: Malcolm makes sure to do everything that was asked of him around the house before heading out.
immoral_action: Malcolm sneaks out right away without finishing any tasks that were asked of him.

situation: Gloria just finished planting some flowers in her garden with her bare hands when her husband lets her know that he made her a sandwich for lunch.
intention: Gloria wants to eat the sandwich for lunch.
moral_action: Gloria goes to the bathroom and washes up before sitting down to eat her sandwich.
immoral_action: Gloria goes into the kitchen and immediately starts eating the sandwich with her hands without washing up first.

situation: Grace is running late when she leaves for work.
intention: Grace wants to minimize the consequences for being late.
moral_action: Grace calls her employer and lets them know she's running a bit late.
immoral_action: Grace speeds in her car and runs through a stop sign in front of a cop.

situation: Peter has a young son named Kyle who is misbehaving.
intention: Peter wants to correct the behavior.
moral_action: Peter calmly reiterates the house rules with Kyle and puts him in a time out.
immoral_action: Peter beats Kyle very severely causing his face and body to be covered in bruises.

situation: Brad is at his desk at work when Ralph comes in wearing really bright yellow pants.
intention: Brad wants to state his surprise at the brightness of Ralph's pants.
moral_action: Brad tells Ralph that he wasn't expecting to see pants that bright but that they make the office pop with good energy.
immoral_action: Brad tells Ralph that the pants are shockingly bright and blinding and that he looks like a moronic clown wearing those to work.

situation: Bailey is talking to her boss Nancy about hiring her boyfriend Jared, and Jared has a criminal past.
intention: Bailey wants Jared to get hired.
moral_action: Bailey sets up a meeting between Jared and Nancy encouraging Jared to be completely honest with her boss.
immoral_action: Bailey praises Jared for being a law-abiding citizen, who never had a run-in with the police, to Nancy, so as to make him look better.

situation: Alan works in an office and has subordinates on his team.
intention: Alan wants to build team rapport.
moral_action: Alan expresses emotion through his face while talking to his subordinates about their interests.
immoral_action: Alan talks to his subordinates about their interests with a stoic face.

situation: Ann's doctor recommends her to get a flu shot so that she can be well protected from the coming flu season.
intention: Ann wants to react to the flu season.
moral_action: Ann gets the flu shot before the flu season comes.
immoral_action: Ann takes vitamin C every day thinking that her immune system will be strong enough to fight the flu.

situation: Sam gets into a heated argument with a group of men at a bar after he accidentally bumps into one of them.
intention: Sam wants to resolve the dispute.
moral_action: Sam defuses the situation with words and offers to buy the men a round of drinks.
immoral_action: Sam starts a fight, kicking and punching the men with his fists.

situation: John has a hard time finding a parking spot close to his office building.
intention: John wants to walk a shorter distance.
moral_action: John gets to work earlier in order to find a good spot.
immoral_action: John borrows his mum's handicapped permit and starts parking next to his building.

situation: Charlotte is dating Logan who has inherited much wealth from his parents, but she is unsure if she feels strong feelings for him.
intention: Charlotte wants to have much wealth.
moral_action: Charlotte decides to focus on her own career and break up with Logan.
immoral_action: Charlotte decides to move into Logan's mansion with him.

situation: John was bored from sitting in Miss Parker's English class.
intention: John wants to get out of class.
moral_action: John raises his hand and asks if he can go to the restroom.
immoral_action: John starts calling the teacher names and mocking and laughing at her.

situation: Donna was looking in the mirror and started to think that she was fat.
intention: Donna wanted to lose weight.
moral_action: Donna starts to eat more fruit and vegetables for her snacks.
immoral_action: Donna starts to skip meals and only drinks water all day.

situation: Nick is standing in line to pay for something when he realizes that his bus is about to leave.
intention: Nick wants to pay for the item immediately.
moral_action: Nick asks the people in front if he can check out now, so he doesn't miss the bus.
immoral_action: Nick walks up to the front of the line and checks out.

situation: John works at an office and is really hungry, and sees a candy bar sitting on the empty desk of a nearby coworker.
intention: John wants to eat.
moral_action: John waits until the coworker comes back and offers to give him a dollar for it.
immoral_action: John grabs the candy bar from the empty desk and eats it.

situation: Eddie has been invited to his friend's birthday party, but he doesn't want to go.
intention: Eddie wants to go to the park.
moral_action: Eddie tells his friend that he had planned on going to the park instead.
immoral_action: Eddie tells his friend he is too sick and goes to the park instead of the birthday party.

situation: Vanessa sits in her car after a fourteen hour shift when her friends ask her if she's still up for going to the bar.
intention: Vanessa wants to relax.
moral_action: Vanessa invites her friends over to her house a quiet evening.
immoral_action: Vanessa does not answer her friends, and she drives home taking a long nap on her bed.

situation: Jared is walking his dog in the dog park and his dog starts to bark and try to run towards a stranger's dog.
intention: Jared wants his dog to enjoy the day in the park.
moral_action: Jared holds tightly onto the leash and reigns in his dog to calm him down.
immoral_action: Jared lets go of the leash and allows his dog to run.

situation: Angie is out with her friends at her local coffee shop, whose boyfriend Angie recently saw make out with another girl.
intention: Angie wants to feel like a good friend.
moral_action: Angie tells her friend her boyfriend has been cheating on her she feels like a good friend.
immoral_action: Angie keeps her knowledge secret from her friend, to make their day together enjoyable for everyone.

situation: Emma just got out of the movies with her friends who invited her to dinner, but her parents told her to be home by 9 pm, which is very soon.
intention: Emma wants to have fun with her friends.
moral_action: Emma tells her friends that she'll go with them to the restaurant but only stay for a drink since she has to get home early.
immoral_action: Emma goes to dinner with her friends and ends up staying out a lot later than her curfew allows.

situation: Jan is standing in her daughter Michelle's room.
intention: Jan wants to clean her daughter's room.
moral_action: Jan asks her daughter if she can clean out her drawers and Michelle says she will do it herself.
immoral_action: Jan goes through Michelle's drawers and throws away things she thinks Michelle doesn't need.

situation: Cindy was at home with her children when her boss calls her into work.
intention: Cindy wants to work.
moral_action: Cindy drops off her children at the babysitter's when she goes to work.
immoral_action: Cindy leaves her children at home when she goes to work.

situation: Jonah's partner Amy has started eating more junk food and stopped exercising which has caused her to gain a lot of weight.
intention: Jonah wants to encourage Amy to lose weight.
moral_action: Jonah invites Amy to join him at the gym and suggests cooking healthy meals together.
immoral_action: Jonah tells Amy that she is getting too big for him to find attractive and that she needs to lose weight if they are going to stay together.

situation: Jack went out to play video games with his friends and told Ann he would be back by midnight.
intention: Jack wants to hang out with friends all night.
moral_action: Jack calls Ann and lets her know he is having fun and wants to stay but didn't want her to worry.
immoral_action: Jack decides he's going to stay at his friends place and not call Ann to tell her.

situation: Ben hardly has any food left until payday, but his friends, Julie and Jim, just showed up to play cards, and he wanted to eat some potato chips.
intention: Ben wants to have a snack.
moral_action: Ben takes out just enough chips for himself, and tells Julie and Jim, he's sorry, but doesn't have anything to offer them,.
immoral_action: Ben dumps the chips into a bowl and tells Julie and Jim to help themselves because he didn't want to feel like a bad host.

situation: Misty is smoking a cigarette during a picnic lunch with her friend, Rita.
intention: Misty wants to share something with Rita.
moral_action: Misty offers Rita some of the potato salad she made.
immoral_action: Misty hands Rita a cigarette multiple times until she gives in and smokes it.

situation: Mark and Natalie have been dating for a while but Natalie's parents don't allow her to stay at his house.
intention: Mark wants to take Natalie on a weekend trip.
moral_action: Mark talks to Natalie's parents and asks for their permission to take Natalie, and they agree with a few stipulations.
immoral_action: Mark tells Natalie not to tell her parents about the trip, and that they will deal with them when they get back.

situation: Ashley has a romantic partner who has been spending a lot of time with a coworker lately.
intention: Ashley wants to express how uncomfortable this makes them feel.
moral_action: Ashley sits down with her partner and explains her feelings.
immoral_action: Ashley demands that her partner immediately cut off all contact with the coworker.

situation: Cindy owns a house and is considering how she wants her things distributed when she dies.
intention: Cindy wants her possessions to go to her children.
moral_action: Cindy makes a will and dictates exactly who gets what when she dies.
immoral_action: Cindy doesn't make a will, knowing that the law will give her things to her children anyway.

situation: Hank's son has been working his first job at a grocery store, and he just received his first pay check.
intention: Hank wants his son to be wise with money.
moral_action: Hank tells his son a story about how far behind he got financially but not being smart with the money he earned when he was younger.
immoral_action: Hank forces his son to put half of his paycheck into savings and pay another twenty percent to him as rent.

situation: Mr. Smith could see that Andy was doing poorly in Algebra, so he offered to tutor Andy and Andy agreed to it.
intention: Andy wants to get better at Algebra.
moral_action: Andy stays after class and gets taught some tips on how to learn Algebra better by Mr. Smith.
immoral_action: Andy decides to study Algebra on his own so that he doesn't have to spend too much time on it.

situation: Hamza needs to pick up a lot of important items at the grocery store.
intention: He wants décide how to go about shopping.
moral_action: He sits down and makes a list, then sticks to it.
immoral_action: Hamza just goes unprepared and figures he can find everything by memory.

situation: Gia who owns a large dog is having guests over to her house.
intention: Gia wants her dog to feel comfortable with guests.
moral_action: Gia uses training techniques to sway her dog every time it starts to make a guest feel uncomfortable.
immoral_action: Gia's dog gets very loud and attentive towards one of the particular guests but Gia insists it is nothing to worry about.

situation: Ruby's daughter was studying for a test that she was going to have in school the next day.
intention: Ruby wanted her daughter to pass the test.
moral_action: Ruby sat with her daughter to help her study for the test.
immoral_action: Ruby sent her daughter to her room to study while she watched her soap operas.

situation: Bill has only been brushing his teeth for a short moment when his arm begins to get tired.
intention: Bill wants to relieve his arm pain.
moral_action: Bill switches hands and brushes his teeth with the other hand as his painful one rests.
immoral_action: Bill stops brushing his teeth and puts his arms down, goes to rest and forgets about brushing.

situation: Mark is the head of the swim team, and a black man wants to join.
intention: Mark wants to say something to the man.
moral_action: Mark asks the man what swim stroke he is best at.
immoral_action: Mark ask the man if he is sure he wants to join the team since he can't swim.

situation: Ginger is a high school senior who has been partaking in many senior pranks and activities.
intention: "Ginger wants to participate in ""senior skip week""."
moral_action: Ginger schedules a doctor's appointment for one day of senior skip week, so she can miss class with a valid excuse.
immoral_action: Ginger and the rest of the seniors skip school for an entire week.

situation: Allan borrows Joe's car and breaks the mirror off putting it in the garage.
intention: Allan wants to avoid trouble with Joe.
moral_action: Allan gets a new mirror and replaces it, telling Joe what happened.
immoral_action: Allan haphazardly glues the mirror back on so that Joe doesn't notice the damage.

situation: Carry is driving her children around town on Halloween night to trick or treat.
intention: Carry wants to take her children trick or treating.
moral_action: Carry walks with her kids to and from houses trick or treating on Halloween night.
immoral_action: Carry takes her kids trick or treating but stays in the car and doesn't pay attention to where her kids are going.

situation: Julie walked in on her boyfriend cheating with another woman.
intention: Julie wants to teach her boyfriend a lesson.
moral_action: Julie tells her boyfriend how much he hurt her and asks how he would feel if she cheated on him.
immoral_action: Julie screams at her boyfriend, throwing a glass at his head.

situation: Laura is suffering emotional abuse at home from her mother.
intention: Laura wants to make the mental pain go away.
moral_action: Laura sees a school counselor and talks with her about her problems.
immoral_action: Laura cuts herself to distract her mind from the emotional suffering.

situation: Thomas is upset that his friend has been ignoring his texts lately.
intention: Thomas wants to call his friend out on it.
moral_action: Thomas calls up his buddy, and asks him if there's a problem between them.
immoral_action: Thomas texts him and insults him a bunch asking what's up.

situation: George and his mother go to the cemetery to visit the grave of George's deceased father, who was not kind to George.
intention: George wants to express how he feels about his father.
moral_action: George decides to focus on the good and tells his mother the things he's grateful for about his father.
immoral_action: George decides to express his displeasure, kicks the headstone repeatedly, and stomps on the grave site.

situation: Ryan is getting ready for work when his coworker and friend Henry calls and asks if Ryan can pick him on his way because his car died.
intention: Ryan wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Ryan only has time to pick up Henry or get breakfast on his way to work, he decides Henry is more important and stops to grab him.
immoral_action: Ryan is running a little late and really wants to grab breakfast on his way to work, so he doesn't pick up Henry and gets breakfast instead.

situation: Ally is working at the perfume counter.
intention: Ally wants to sell perfume.
moral_action: Ally approaches a customer and asks if they would like to smell a sample on paper.
immoral_action: Ally sees a potential customer approaching and sprays them with perfume.

situation: Josephine is on a school field trip to NYC, and her mother gave her a credit card to use for emergencies only.
intention: Josephine wants to purchase souvenirs with her mother's credit card.
moral_action: Josephine calls her mom to ask if it is okay that she buys some souvenirs.
immoral_action: Josephine goes on a shopping spree with her mom's card.

situation: Tim and Jamal just sat down to eat lunch in the school cafeteria.
intention: Tim wants to make Jamal laugh.
moral_action: Tim decides against something drastic and tells Jamal a funny joke he heard on TV the night before.
immoral_action: Tim walks over to the ketchup container, pulls his pants down, and rubs his Johnson all over the condiments.

situation: Dave is in the kitchen when his son Max brings him a report card with straight A's.
intention: Dave wants to say something to Max about the report card.
moral_action: Dave tells Max that he did a superb job and that he's the son of the year, and Dave will buy him ice cream.
immoral_action: Dave tells Max that he did what he was supposed to and now he has to work even harder to do it again next year.

situation: Ella is starting a new brand to sell her creations.
intention: Ella wants an attractive logo that she can use to market.
moral_action: Ella hires a designer to make a logo for her.
immoral_action: Ella copies an artist's drawing from their website and edits it slightly to use as a logo.

situation: Bobby and Jane are discussing her recent depression and struggles that she has been going through.
intention: Bobby wants to offer his perspective of her situation to offer insight.
moral_action: Bobby listens to Jane's problem, offering his perspective on how she can work on her depression giving her ideas to use.
immoral_action: Bobby offers his perspective on Jane's problems and tells her to suck it up or stop bringing her problems up.

situation: Ken is speeding down the freeway because he wants to get home early, and he's pulled over by officer Pete.
intention: Ken wants to explain why he went so fast.
moral_action: Ken tells Pete that he was being an idiot and trying to get home early, and he's really sorry he won't do it again.
immoral_action: Ken tells Pete that his wife texted him about an emergency, and he's just rushing home.

situation: Billy threw a rock at a classmate during recess and was given detention after school as a punishment.
intention: Billy wants watch his favorite baseball team after school.
moral_action: Billy goes to detention and asks if the teacher could provide updates on the score of his favorite baseball team.
immoral_action: Billy skips detention and goes home to watch his favorite baseball team on television.

situation: James and his girlfriend have been fighting about money a lot recently, and James just found out she spent $150 eating at restaurants this week.
intention: James wants to convince his girlfriend to spend less money.
moral_action: James asks his girlfriend to create a separate bank account, so they can each manage their own spending money.
immoral_action: James punches his girlfriend and says he'll beat her every time she goes to a restaurant.

situation: Mark goes out clubbing and meets a girl that he is interested in named Rose.
intention: Mark wants Rose to come home with him.
moral_action: Mark invites Rose to a nightcap at his place.
immoral_action: Mark spikes Rose's drink so that she is more likely to go home with him.

situation: Nicole and her husband Mike are having a disagreement.
intention: Nicole wants to win the disagreement.
moral_action: Nicole calmly explains the reasons why she thinks she is right.
immoral_action: Nicole shouts at Mike, hoping to intimidate him by raising her voice.

situation: Diana is watching her son at home because his school was experiencing a snow day.
intention: Diana wants her son to play outside.
moral_action: Diana asks her son if he wants to go outside with her to build a snowman.
immoral_action: Diana tells her son that he's being annoying and to go outside, then forgets to unlock the door for him to come inside.

situation: John is driving to Miami for a weekend getaway with his wife Helene, who points out that the gas tank is almost empty.
intention: John wants to respond to Helene.
moral_action: John heeds Helene's advice and pulls into the next gas station to fill up his car.
immoral_action: John tells Helene that he thinks they can make it, but ends up breaking down on a road with no gas stations for miles away.

situation: Luke is a fifth-grader with a big crush on his class' prettiest girl.
intention: Luke wants his crush to notice him.
moral_action: Luke starts talking with his crush and tells her funny and surprising stories.
immoral_action: At recess, Luke approaches his crush and suddenly yanks her hair.

situation: James is playing poker with some friends after work.
intention: James wants to win enough money to buy a new pair of shoes.
moral_action: James plays a fair game of poke.
immoral_action: James hides an Ace in his sleeve and switches it with a card in his hand, giving him 4 of a kind.

situation: Jake and his friend Luke are at a baseball game when Luke turns to Jake and says the game is boring, and they should leave.
intention: Jake wants to respond to Luke's statement.
moral_action: Jake tells Luke that he's right and the game is a total snoozefest, and he wants to leave as well.
immoral_action: Jake tells Luke that he's crazy because the game is not boring at all, but he can leave alone if he wants to.

situation: The Fourth of July is coming up, and it's Evan's turn to have family over for a holiday.
intention: Evan wants to celebrate the Fourth of July.
moral_action: Evan invites his family over for a barbecue on the Fourth.
immoral_action: Evan celebrates the Fourth by himself by watching fireworks on TV.

situation: Scott went through a traumatic experience and is now depressed.
intention: Scott wants to deal with the emotional pain.
moral_action: Scott sees a therapist to help him deal with the traumatic experience.
immoral_action: Scott becomes obsessed with dying and tells people about his intentions to commit suicide.

situation: Ellie has invited Josh over to her birthday party at her house.
intention: Josh wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Josh goes to the party and brings Ellie a board game for a gift.
immoral_action: Josh goes to the party without a gift and eats several pieces of cake.

situation: Melissa breaks a lamp she's had for years, then remembers that the store she bought it from has a generous lifetime return policy.
intention: Melissa wants to go to the store she bought the lamp from.
moral_action: Melissa goes to the store she bought the lamp from to purchase a similar one.
immoral_action: Melissa brings the broken lamp to the store and demands a refund.

situation: Tim invites Dylan over to his house, and they are about to sit down in the den.
intention: Tim wants Dylan to have fun at his house.
moral_action: Tim offers Dylan the comfy chair and asks Dylan what game to play first.
immoral_action: Tim immediately sits in the comfy chair while thinking of games to play with Dylan.

situation: James is driving when Keith who was riding a bike cuts him off.
intention: James wants to react angrily to Keith's cut off.
moral_action: James speeds up his car to catch up to Keith and then flips him the finger before driving off.
immoral_action: James speeds up his car and slams into the back of Keith's' bike knocking him down and running him over.

situation: Jacob has a late final exam that's at the same time as when his friends are going to beach week.
intention: Jacob wants to be able to go to beach week with everyone else.
moral_action: Jacob talked to the professor to see if he could take the exam at an earlier date.
immoral_action: Jacob skips the exam to go to the beach, assuming that his grades leading up to the final would be enough to pass.

situation: Deacon was angry because of a stressful day at work that day.
intention: Deacon wants to calm down at home.
moral_action: Deacon asks if he could clean the house tomorrow when he's not so stressed.
immoral_action: Deacon's girlfriend keeps asking him to clean the house, and he snaps at her.

situation: Blake sits on the couch after a stressful day at work.
intention: Blake wants to relax.
moral_action: Blake decides to do meditation exercises with new age music in the background.
immoral_action: Blake relaxes by smoking one of his old cigars.

situation: John's brother decides to take a risk to start his own business.
intention: John wants to talk to his brother about the decision.
moral_action: John praises his brother for starting a business and offers to help.
immoral_action: John berates his brother for taking the risk to start a business.

situation: Jesse and Zack are recently divorced and Jesse still has Zack's photo's.
intention: Zack wants to try and get his pictures from Jesse.
moral_action: Zack sends a text message to ask for his photos, but Jesse doesn't respond, so Zack decides to wait for a response.
immoral_action: Zack sends a text message to ask for his photos and when Jesse doesn't respond, he calls her at work.

situation: Paul recently caught his underaged son smoking a cigarette and is outraged.
intention: Paul wants to address his son.
moral_action: Paul expresses his disappointment in his son and grounds him for two weeks.
immoral_action: Paul loudly confronts his son and hits him until he bleeds.

situation: Al wakes up and realizes that it's election day.
intention: Al wants to decide whether to vote today.
moral_action: Al gets out and votes for the policies he believes in at the voting booth.
immoral_action: Al doesn't vote because there is no way [unpopular politician] can possibly win.

situation: Don has a dog that has just torn his couch apart when left alone at home.
intention: Don wants to teach the dog not to damage the furniture.
moral_action: Don uses a scented product which is offensive to dog noses on the furniture.
immoral_action: Don closes the dog in a room as a form of discipline.

situation: Linda would love to have a cookout over the coming weekend, but isn't sure.
intention: Linda has to decide whether to have a cookout or rest over the weekend.
moral_action: Linda spends her energy inviting people over for a cookout and asks everyone to bring something.
immoral_action: Linda settles in with movies and popcorn for the whole weekend and doesn't have any friends over.

situation: Doug's neighbor hasn't fed or let their dog inside in over a 3 weeks.
intention: Doug wants to check on the dog.
moral_action: Doug goes towards the dog and sees that he is extremely thin, then unchains him and puts him in his vehicle to get him help.
immoral_action: Doug approaches the dog and notices clear signs of abuse and neglect, but walks away afraid of confrontation.

situation: Mary is at her new friend Gina's house and is getting bored waiting for Gina to prepare and bring some snacks.
intention: Mary wants to kill some time.
moral_action: Mary goes to the kitchen and offers to help Gina out with the snacks.
immoral_action: Mary opens up Gina's desk drawers and looks around to see what's inside them.

situation: Donald sees a computer game he really wants at his best friend John's house.
intention: Donald wants to take the game home to play it.
moral_action: Donald asks John if he can borrow the game for a few weeks.
immoral_action: Donald puts the game in his backpack without telling John.

situation: Jim has moved into a small apartment.

situation: Adam is talking to Jill when Jill realizes she lost her wallet.

situation: Billy's grandmother is having a birthday party at the same time as a football game.

situation: Fred hates his job and sometimes does what he wants instead of what he should be doing.
